# login_game_stores

[← Command index](README.md)

Log in to the selected game stores so their purchases, metadata and downloads can be fetched.

## Synopsis

```
login_game_stores [options]
```

## Description

Picks stores by category and subcategory (for example `-c Computer -s Steam`); with no
selection it goes through every subcategory. Subcategories without a store are skipped.
For each store that is not already logged in, it runs the store's own command-line
login, such as SteamCMD for Steam or Legendary for Epic Games, which may prompt for
credentials.

The session it leaves behind is what `build_game_store_purchases`,
`build_game_metadata_files` and `download_game_metadata_assets` use when they talk
to a store.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-u, --game_supercategory <game_supercategory>` | Supercategory of the stores. Default: `Roms`. Allowed: `Assets`, `Emulators`, `Roms`, `DLC`, `Updates`, `Tags`, `Saves`, `Setup`, `Installs`. |
| `-c, --game_category <game_category>` | Category of the stores to log in to; all categories when omitted. Allowed: `Computer`, `Microsoft`, `Nintendo`, `Other`, `Sony`. |
| `-s, --game_subcategory <game_subcategory>` | Store subcategory, such as `Steam` or `GOG`; every subcategory of the selected categories when omitted. ### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Log in to Steam

```bash
login_game_stores -c Computer -s Steam
```

### Log in to the Epic Games store

```bash
login_game_stores -c Computer -s "Epic Games"
```

### Log in to every store

```bash
login_game_stores
```

## Notes

- Stores sit under the `Roms` supercategory, which is the default, so `-u` is not needed.
- The store's login tool must be installed first; `setup_tools` installs them.
